IN PHOTOS | Students, faculty, and staff of the University of the Philippines Diliman converged at the Palma Hall steps on Friday (September 12) for a campus-wide Black Friday Protest, denouncing corruption, construction delays, and sweeping budget cuts.

The university incurred a ₱2.08-billion reduction in its 2025 budget—the steepest in two decades. For 2026, the Department of Budget and Management has proposed a ₱25.82-billion allocation for UP, just about half of the funding the institution had sought. | via Rex Espiritu 

📷 UJP UPD

For more news updates, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI.

Speakers representing each college denounces the lavish lifestyles of corrupt officials while students and the public bear the brunt by high out-of-pocket expensiture for basic social services such as education and health.

The hundred-strong participants are set to join the students of the College of Arts and Science to continue the protest.

The protesters urged the government to hold officials accountable for anomalies in flood control projects and demanded a higher education budget amid massive cuts and unfinished infrastructure. 

📸: Santi San Juan/MB

#MSNews | The Las Piñas City government has acquired garbage collection equipment to improve waste management and clearing operations and reduce the risk of flooding.

On Friday, Mayor April Aguilar and Vice Mayor Mel Aguilar attended the blessing ceremony and handed over the newly acquired vehicles to the City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO).

The fleet comprises seven compactor trucks designated for garbage collection, two dump trucks intended for transporting debris and bulky waste, and one boom crane for clearing operations. | via Joel Zurbano

📷Las Piñas LGU
